# 1 Enoch Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**1** This is the book of Enoch's righteous words — his reprimand to the eternal Watchers, delivered at the command of the Holy and Great One in a vision.

**2** What I saw in my sleep I will now put into words — using this tongue of flesh and this breath that God gave humans for speaking and for understanding with the heart.

**3** Just as God created humanity with the ability to grasp wisdom, so he created me and commissioned me to deliver this rebuke to the Watchers, those sons of heaven.

**4** I wrote your petition down. But my vision made this clear: your petition will never be granted — not for all eternity. Final judgment has been passed on you. It will not be granted.

**5** From now on, you will never ascend to heaven again. The decree has been issued to chain you in the earth for every generation to come.

**6** But first, you will watch your beloved sons destroyed. You will take no joy in them — they will fall before you in battle.

**7** No prayer of theirs will help them, and no prayer of yours will help you — even if you weep and beg and recite every word I have written down.

**8** Then the vision took hold of me: clouds beckoned, mist called to me, and the stars and lightning swept me along. The wind lifted me up and carried me into heaven.

**9** I came to a wall made of crystal, ringed with tongues of fire. Terror gripped me.

**10** I walked through the fire and approached a vast house built entirely of crystal. Its walls were like a mosaic of crystal tiles, and even its foundation was crystal.

**11** The ceiling looked like the night sky — star-paths and lightning — with fiery cherubim woven among them, and their heaven was clear as still water.

**12** Blazing fire ringed the walls, and fire roared through its gates.

**13** I walked inside. It was furnace-hot and ice-cold at the same time. There was nothing in it to comfort a living being. Fear overwhelmed me; I shook uncontrollably.

**14** Trembling, I collapsed facedown.

**15** Then I saw it — a second house, far greater than the first. Its door stood wide open before me, and the whole structure was built of living flame.

**16** Its glory, its grandeur, its sheer scale — I have no words to describe it.

**17** The floor was fire. Above it, lightning and star-tracks blazed, and the ceiling too was a canopy of flame.

**18** Inside I saw a towering throne. It looked like crystal; its wheels shone like the sun. And I could see the shapes of cherubim.

**19** Rivers of fire poured out from beneath the throne — so intense I could not look directly at it.

**20** The Great Glory sat on the throne. His robe blazed brighter than the sun and was whiter than any snow.

**21** No angel could enter that room or look at his face — the glory was too overwhelming. No living thing could bear the sight.

**22** Fire encircled him. A great fire stood before him. No one nearby could approach. Ten thousand times ten thousand stood in his presence, yet he had no need of any advisor.

**23** The holiest ones who stood nearest to him never left — not by night, not ever.

**24** I had been facedown the entire time, shaking. Then the Lord himself spoke to me: 'Come closer, Enoch. Hear my word.'

**25** One of the holy ones came to me, woke me, and helped me to my feet. He brought me to the door. I bowed my face low.


---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering aimed at modern English readability. Ge'ez idioms are rendered by their functional English equivalents. Theological terms are translated for impact rather than etymological precision.*
